# What EpiExposure does?

`Introduzir o usuário ao workflow básico: da exposição ao modelo.`

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# =========================================================
# SIMULACAO: 520 epidemias x 86 dias
# 1 severidade por epidemia (DLNM-style)
# =========================================================

set.seed(123)

# -----------------------------
# Dimensoes
# -----------------------------
n_epi  <- 520
n_days <- 86   # 0–85

# -----------------------------
# Estrutura base (long format)
# -----------------------------
sim_data <- expand.grid(
  epi_id = 1:n_epi,
  dpp    = 0:(n_days - 1)
)

sim_data <- sim_data[order(sim_data$epi_id, sim_data$dpp), ]

# -----------------------------
# Inicializar
# -----------------------------
sim_data$tmean <- NA
sim_data$rain  <- NA
sim_data$rh    <- NA

# vetor final de severidade (1 por epi)
y_epi <- numeric(n_epi)

# =========================================================
# LOOP POR EPIDEMIA
# =========================================================

for (i in 1:n_epi) {

  idx <- sim_data$epi_id == i
  t_seq <- 0:(n_days - 1)

  # -----------------------------
  # Clima
  # -----------------------------
  tmean <- 25 + 5*sin(2*pi*t_seq/85) + rnorm(n_days, 0, 1.5)
  rh    <- 70 + 10*sin(2*pi*t_seq/85 + 1) + rnorm(n_days, 0, 4)
  rain  <- rpois(n_days, lambda = 3)

  # -----------------------------
  # ESTRUTURA DE LAG (CHAVE)
  # -----------------------------

  # efeito temperatura: forte em lags 5–20
  w_temp <- dnorm(t_seq, mean = 12, sd = 6)

  temp_effect <- sum(
    dnorm(tmean, mean = 25, sd = 4) * w_temp
  )

  # efeito chuva: acumulado em lags 10–30
  w_rain <- dnorm(t_seq, mean = 20, sd = 8)

  rain_effect <- sum(rain * w_rain)

  # efeito umidade: mais difuso
  w_rh <- dnorm(t_seq, mean = 15, sd = 10)

  rh_effect <- sum((rh - 60)/40 * w_rh)

  # -----------------------------
  # COMBINACAO FINAL (linear predictor)
  # -----------------------------
  eta <- 
    0.6 * temp_effect +
    0.2 * rain_effect +
    0.2 * rh_effect

  # -----------------------------
  # Converter para proporção (logit)
  # -----------------------------
  y_val <- 1 / (1 + exp(-eta/10 + rnorm(1, 0, 0.3)))

  # limitar
  y_val <- max(min(y_val, 0.95), 0.001)

  # -----------------------------
  # salvar
  # -----------------------------
  sim_data$tmean[idx] <- tmean
  sim_data$rain[idx]  <- rain
  sim_data$rh[idx]    <- rh

  y_epi[i] <- y_val
}

# =========================================================
# JUNTAR SEVERIDADE (1 por epi)
# =========================================================

y_df <- data.frame(
  epi_id = 1:n_epi,
  y = y_epi
)

sim_data <- merge(sim_data, y_df, by = "epi_id")

# ordenar novamente
sim_data <- sim_data[order(sim_data$epi_id, sim_data$dpp), ]

# =========================================================
# RESULTADO
# =========================================================

head(sim_data)

# checagem
table(table(sim_data$epi_id))   # deve dar 86 por epi
length(unique(sim_data$epi_id)) # 520 epidemias
```
# ARTIGO
```{r}
# =============================================================
# SIMULACAO DLNM COM TRES VARIAVEIS
#
# 520 epidemias x 86 dias
# Uma severidade final por epidemia
#
# Variaveis:
#   1. Temperatura media
#   2. Molhamento foliar
#   3. Chuva
#
# Desfecho:
#   Severidade final, como proporcao entre 0 e 1
# =============================================================

set.seed(123)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Pacotes
# -------------------------------------------------------------

library(dlnm)
library(splines)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Dimensoes
# -------------------------------------------------------------

n_epi  <- 520
n_days <- 86

dpp_values <- 0:(n_days - 1)
lag_values <- 0:(n_days - 1)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Matrizes de exposicao
#
# Linhas:
#   epidemias
#
# Colunas:
#   DPP 0 a 85
# -------------------------------------------------------------

tmean_dpp <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_epi,
  ncol = n_days
)

wetness_dpp <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_epi,
  ncol = n_days
)

rain_dpp <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_epi,
  ncol = n_days
)

colnames(tmean_dpp) <- paste0("dpp_", dpp_values)
colnames(wetness_dpp) <- paste0("dpp_", dpp_values)
colnames(rain_dpp) <- paste0("dpp_", dpp_values)

# =============================================================
# 1. SIMULAR OS HISTORICOS CLIMATICOS
# =============================================================

for (i in seq_len(n_epi)) {

  # -----------------------------------------------------------
  # Variacao entre epidemias
  #
  # Cada epidemia recebe condicoes climaticas medias diferentes.
  # Essa variacao entre epidemias e essencial, pois o desfecho
  # possui somente uma observacao por epidemia.
  # -----------------------------------------------------------

  temp_shift <- rnorm(
    1,
    mean = 0,
    sd = 2.2
  )

  wetness_shift <- rnorm(
    1,
    mean = 0,
    sd = 3.0
  )

  rain_shift <- rnorm(
    1,
    mean = 0,
    sd = 0.45
  )

  # -----------------------------------------------------------
  # Componentes temporalmente autocorrelacionados
  # -----------------------------------------------------------

  ar_temp <- as.numeric(
    arima.sim(
      model = list(ar = 0.70),
      n = n_days,
      sd = 1.1
    )
  )

  ar_wetness <- as.numeric(
    arima.sim(
      model = list(ar = 0.75),
      n = n_days,
      sd = 1.7
    )
  )

  ar_rain <- as.numeric(
    arima.sim(
      model = list(ar = 0.55),
      n = n_days,
      sd = 0.55
    )
  )

  # -----------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. TEMPERATURA MEDIA
  # -----------------------------------------------------------

  tmean <- (
    25 +
    temp_shift +
    3.5 * sin(
      2 * pi * dpp_values / 85 +
      runif(1, -0.35, 0.35)
    ) +
    ar_temp
  )

  # Restringir aos limites utilizados na simulacao
  tmean <- pmin(
    pmax(tmean, 15),
    36
  )

  # -----------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. MOLHAMENTO FOLIAR
  # -----------------------------------------------------------

  wetness <- (
    10 +
    wetness_shift +
    2.2 * sin(
      2 * pi * dpp_values / 48 +
      runif(1, -0.50, 0.50)
    ) +
    ar_wetness
  )

  # Horas por dia: intervalo fisico de 0 a 24
  wetness <- pmin(
    pmax(wetness, 0),
    24
  )

  # -----------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. CHUVA
  #
  # Primeiro e simulada uma probabilidade diaria de chuva.
  # Quando ocorre chuva, a quantidade e simulada por uma
  # distribuicao Gamma.
  # -----------------------------------------------------------

  rain_probability <- plogis(
    -0.75 +
    rain_shift +
    0.45 * sin(
      2 * pi * dpp_values / 37 +
      runif(1, -0.50, 0.50)
    ) +
    ar_rain
  )

  rainy_day <- rbinom(
    n = n_days,
    size = 1,
    prob = rain_probability
  )

  rain_amount <- rgamma(
    n = n_days,
    shape = 1.8,
    scale = 5
  )

  rain <- rainy_day * rain_amount

  # Limitar eventos extremos para estabilizar o exemplo
  rain <- pmin(
    rain,
    40
  )

  # -----------------------------------------------------------
  # Salvar as series
  # -----------------------------------------------------------

  tmean_dpp[i, ] <- tmean
  wetness_dpp[i, ] <- wetness
  rain_dpp[i, ] <- rain
}

# =============================================================
# 2. CONVERTER DPP EM LAG
# =============================================================
#
# A severidade final e observada aos 85 DPP.
#
# Portanto:
#
# DPP 85 = lag 0
# DPP 84 = lag 1
# DPP 83 = lag 2
# ...
# DPP  0 = lag 85
#
# O crossbasis espera:
#
# coluna 1 = lag 0
# coluna 2 = lag 1
# ...
# coluna 86 = lag 85
#
# Por isso, as colunas das matrizes sao invertidas.
# =============================================================

tmean_lag <- tmean_dpp[, n_days:1, drop = FALSE]
wetness_lag <- wetness_dpp[, n_days:1, drop = FALSE]
rain_lag <- rain_dpp[, n_days:1, drop = FALSE]

colnames(tmean_lag) <- paste0("lag_", lag_values)
colnames(wetness_lag) <- paste0("lag_", lag_values)
colnames(rain_lag) <- paste0("lag_", lag_values)

# =============================================================
# 3. RELACAO EXPOSICAO-RESPOSTA VERDADEIRA
# =============================================================

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.1 Temperatura
#
# Resposta unimodal:
#   maior favorabilidade proxima de 26 graus C
# -------------------------------------------------------------

temp_response <- exp(
  -0.5 * ((tmean_lag - 26) / 3.0)^2
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.2 Molhamento foliar
#
# Resposta sigmoide:
#   aumento acentuado acima de aproximadamente 11 horas
# -------------------------------------------------------------

wetness_response <- plogis(
  (wetness_lag - 11) / 1.7
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.3 Chuva
#
# Resposta crescente com saturacao.
#
# sqrt() reduz a influencia de eventos extremos e permite que
# chuvas moderadas ja produzam aumento de favorabilidade.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

rain_response <- plogis(
  (sqrt(rain_lag) - 2.2) / 0.75
)

# =============================================================
# 4. FUNCOES VERDADEIRAS DE LAG
# =============================================================

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Temperatura:
#   janela mais tardia
#   maior contribuicao proxima ao lag 18
# -------------------------------------------------------------

temp_lag_weights <- dnorm(
  lag_values,
  mean = 18,
  sd = 9
)

temp_lag_weights <- (
  temp_lag_weights /
  sum(temp_lag_weights)
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Molhamento foliar:
#   janela intermediaria
#   maior contribuicao proxima ao lag 27
# -------------------------------------------------------------

wetness_lag_weights <- dnorm(
  lag_values,
  mean = 27,
  sd = 11
)

wetness_lag_weights <- (
  wetness_lag_weights /
  sum(wetness_lag_weights)
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Chuva:
#   efeito mais recente
#   maior contribuicao proxima ao lag 10
# -------------------------------------------------------------

rain_lag_weights <- dnorm(
  lag_values,
  mean = 10,
  sd = 7
)

rain_lag_weights <- (
  rain_lag_weights /
  sum(rain_lag_weights)
)

# =============================================================
# 5. EFEITOS CUMULATIVOS VERDADEIROS
# =============================================================

true_temp_effect <- as.numeric(
  temp_response %*% temp_lag_weights
)

true_wetness_effect <- as.numeric(
  wetness_response %*% wetness_lag_weights
)

true_rain_effect <- as.numeric(
  rain_response %*% rain_lag_weights
)

# =============================================================
# 6. PADRONIZAR OS EFEITOS
# =============================================================
#
# A padronizacao permite controlar diretamente a magnitude
# relativa de cada exposicao no preditor linear.
# =============================================================

temp_effect_z <- as.numeric(
  scale(true_temp_effect)
)

wetness_effect_z <- as.numeric(
  scale(true_wetness_effect)
)

rain_effect_z <- as.numeric(
  scale(true_rain_effect)
)

# =============================================================
# 7. GERAR A SEVERIDADE FINAL
# =============================================================
#
# As tres variaveis possuem contribuicao para a severidade.
#
# Molhamento:
#   efeito mais forte
#
# Temperatura:
#   efeito intermediario
#
# Chuva:
#   efeito ligeiramente menor, mas ainda suficientemente forte
#   para ser detectado no teste global.
# =============================================================

eta_true <- (
  -1.10 +
  0.95 * temp_effect_z +
  1.10 * wetness_effect_z +
  0.75 * rain_effect_z
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Erro residual
#
# Quanto menor o sigma_error, maior sera o desempenho preditivo.
#
# Sugestao para exemplo do pacote:
#   0.10 a 0.15 = desempenho elevado
#   0.20 a 0.30 = exemplo mais desafiador
# -------------------------------------------------------------

sigma_error <- 0.12

eta_observed <- (
  eta_true +
  rnorm(
    n_epi,
    mean = 0,
    sd = sigma_error
  )
)

y_epi <- plogis(eta_observed)

# =============================================================
# 8. CRIAR CONJUNTO DE DADOS LONG
# =============================================================

sim_data <- data.frame(
  epi_id = rep(
    seq_len(n_epi),
    each = n_days
  ),

  dpp = rep(
    dpp_values,
    times = n_epi
  ),

  lag = rep(
    rev(lag_values),
    times = n_epi
  ),

  tmean = as.vector(
    t(tmean_dpp)
  ),

  wetness = as.vector(
    t(wetness_dpp)
  ),

  rain = as.vector(
    t(rain_dpp)
  ),

  y = rep(
    y_epi,
    each = n_days
  )
)

sim_data <- sim_data[
  order(
    sim_data$epi_id,
    sim_data$dpp
  ),
]

rownames(sim_data) <- NULL

# =============================================================
# 9. CHECAGENS DA SIMULACAO
# =============================================================

head(sim_data)
tail(sim_data)

# Deve retornar:
# 86 520
table(
  table(sim_data$epi_id)
)

# Deve retornar 520
length(
  unique(sim_data$epi_id)
)

# Cada epidemia deve possuir apenas uma severidade
severity_per_epidemic <- tapply(
  sim_data$y,
  sim_data$epi_id,
  function(x) length(unique(x))
)

if (!all(severity_per_epidemic == 1)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Erro na simulacao: pelo menos uma epidemia possui ",
      "mais de um valor de severidade."
    )
  )
}

# Verificar valores ausentes
if (anyNA(sim_data)) {
  stop(
    "A simulacao produziu valores ausentes."
  )
}

# Verificar limites da severidade
if (any(sim_data$y <= 0 | sim_data$y >= 1)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "A severidade deve estar estritamente entre 0 e 1 ",
      "para a transformacao logit."
    )
  )
}

# Resumos
summary(sim_data$tmean)
summary(sim_data$wetness)
summary(sim_data$rain)
summary(y_epi)

# Correlacao entre os efeitos cumulativos verdadeiros
effect_correlation <- cor(
  cbind(
    temperature = temp_effect_z,
    wetness = wetness_effect_z,
    rain = rain_effect_z
  )
)

print(
  round(effect_correlation, 3)
)

# Distribuicao da severidade
hist(
  y_epi,
  breaks = 25,
  main = "Distribuicao da severidade simulada",
  xlab = "Severidade",
  col = "gray80",
  border = "white"
)

```

```{r}
wetness_plot = sim_data%>%
```

```{r}

sim_data2 = sim_data |> 
  filter(epi_id <= 480)

sim_data3 = sim_data |> 
  filter(!epi_id <= 480)

sim_data2$epi_id = as.factor(sim_data2$epi_id)
sim_data3$epi_id = as.factor(sim_data3$epi_id)

### train

cb <- define_exposure(
  data = sim_data2,
  vars = c("wetness","tmean","rain"),
  lag_max = 85,
  df_var = 3,
  df_lag = 2
)

dat <- build_design(
  data = sim_data2,
  cb_templates = cb,
  lag_max = 85
)

dat <- prepare_response(data = dat, y_var = "y", family = "beta")

fit <- fit_epidlnm(
  data = dat,
  model_engine = "glmmTMB",
  family = "beta",
  random_effect = NULL,
  epiexposure_spec = attr(cb, "spec")
)

fit$sdr$pdHess
range(dat$y_model)
sum(dat$y_model <= 0)

sum(dat$y_model >= 1)

any(is.na(vcov(fit)$cond))


###  test

cb2 <- define_exposure(
  data = sim_data3,
  vars = c("wetness","tmean","rain"),
  lag_max = 85,
  df_var = 3,
  df_lag = 2
)

dat2 <- build_design(
  data = sim_data3,
  cb_templates = cb,
  lag_max = 85
)

dat2 <- prepare_response(data = dat2, y_var = "y", family = "beta")


summary(fit)

t = predict(fit, newdata = dat2, type = "response",allow.new.levels=TRUE)


dat3 = dat2
dat3$t = t


dat3 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(y,t))+
  geom_point(color = "#C44E52", size = 2)+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F, color = "#55A868", linewidth = 1.4)+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(x = "Observed (proportion)",
       y = "Predicted (proportion)")+
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,0.80), expand = c(0.01,0.01))+
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,0.80), expand = c(0.01,0.01))

CCC(dat3$y, dat3$t, ci = "z-transform", conf.level = 0.95, na.rm = FALSE)
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}


cb <- define_exposure(
  wx_long = sim_data,
  vars = c("cum", "rh", "tmean"),
  lag_max = 85,
  df_var = 4,
  df_lag = 2
)

```


```{r}

# construir design matrix
dat <- build_design(
  wx_long = sim_data,
  cb_templates = cb,
  lag_max = 85
)

```
```{r}
check_identifiability(wx_long = sim_data, var = "cum",
                      df_var = 2, df_lag = 2, lag_max = 85)
```


```{r}

# preparar resposta
dat <- prepare_response(dat = dat, y_var = "y", family = "beta")

```


```{r}



# ajustar modelo
fit <- fit_epidlnm(
  dat = dat,
  model_engine = "glmmTMB",
  family = "beta",
  random_effect = "epi_id",
  epiexposure_spec = attr(cb, "spec")
)

summary(fit)
t = predict(fit, newdata = dat, type = "response")


dat2 = dat
dat2$t = t


dat2 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(y,t))+
  geom_point()



sim_dataa = sim_data %>% 
  filter(epi_id <= 80)

best <- find_bestfit(
  epi_data = sim_dataa,
  response = "y",
  group = "epi_id",
  time = "dpp",
  vars = c("tmean", "rh"),
  lag_max = 85,
  df_var_grid = c(2),
  df_lag_grid = c(2),
  max_vars = 2,
  model_engine = "glmmTMB",
  family = "beta",
  verbose = TRUE
)

sim_data

ens_unweighted <- ensemble_bestfit(
  bestfit = best,
  method = "unweighted",
  top_n = 10
)


ens_weighted <- ensemble_bestfit(
  bestfit = best,
  method = "weighted",
  top_n = 10,
  weight_metric = "CCC",
  weight_transform = "softmax"
)


ens_best <- ensemble_bestfit(
  bestfit = best,
  method = "hard_voting",
  top_n = 10
)


ens_stacked <- ensemble_bestfit(
  bestfit = best,
  method = "stacked",
  top_n = 10,
  stacking_model = "ridge",
  lambda = 1e-4
)
```

```{r}
best_model_id <- best$model_id[1]

best_lag <- ens$lag_data |>
  dplyr::filter(model_id == best_model_id) |>
  dplyr::select(
    var,
    lag,
    best_model_contribution = contribution
  )

ensemble_lag <- ens$ensemble_by_lag |>
  dplyr::select(
    var,
    lag,
    ensemble_contribution,
    ensemble_percent_contribution
  )

lag_compare <- dplyr::left_join(
  best_lag,
  ensemble_lag,
  by = c("var", "lag")
)

lag_compare
```

```{r}
lag_compare <- lag_compare |>
  dplyr::group_by(var) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    best_model_percent_contribution =
      100 * abs(best_model_contribution) /
      sum(abs(best_model_contribution), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

plot_df <- lag_compare |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(best_model_contribution, ensemble_contribution),
    names_to = "source",
    values_to = "contribution"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    source = dplyr::recode(
      source,
      best_model_contribution = "Best model",
      ensemble_contribution = "Lag ensemble"
    )
  )

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = lag, y = contribution, color = source)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ var, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Lag",
    y = "Lag-specific contribution",
    color = NULL,
    title = "Lag-specific contribution: best model vs lag ensemble"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
plot_pct <- lag_compare |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(best_model_percent_contribution, ensemble_percent_contribution),
    names_to = "source",
    values_to = "percent_contribution"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    source = dplyr::recode(
      source,
      best_model_percent_contribution = "Best model",
      ensemble_percent_contribution = "Lag ensemble"
    )
  )

ggplot(plot_pct, aes(x = lag, y = percent_contribution, color = source)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ var, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Lag",
    y = "Relative contribution (%)",
    color = NULL,
    title = "Relative lag importance: best model vs lag ensemble"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
lag_distance <- lag_compare |>
  dplyr::group_by(var) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    rmse_contribution = sqrt(mean(
      (best_model_contribution - ensemble_contribution)^2,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )),
    correlation = stats::cor(
      best_model_contribution,
      ensemble_contribution,
      use = "complete.obs"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

lag_distance
```

```{r}
lag_compare |>
  dplyr::filter(var == "rain") |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    min_best = min(best_model_contribution, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_best = max(best_model_contribution, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_ensemble = min(ensemble_contribution, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_ensemble = max(ensemble_contribution, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_abs_best = mean(abs(best_model_contribution), na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_abs_ensemble = mean(abs(ensemble_contribution), na.rm = TRUE),
    rmse_relative_to_best =
      sqrt(mean((best_model_contribution - ensemble_contribution)^2, na.rm = TRUE)) /
      mean(abs(best_model_contribution), na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```
